subject: Route-level insights / attribution request from Acme AI

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Route-level insights / attribution request from Acme AI

Team — quick context and ask from Acme AI (discovery this week). They want the ability to see cost and p95 latency broken down by request "route" (their internal routing name that maps to our endpoint path + model variant) and to export per-route usage for invoicing/chargeback. Key asks: 
- per-route token & cost breakdown (daily)
- p50/p95 latency per route (rolling 7/30d)
- mapping table: route -> model_variant -> engine_id for accurate attribution

I attached a sample of their export (acme_route_sample.csv) and highlighted 4 routes they care about. Customer is asking for an ETA/prototype — they prefer CSV exports now and a dashboard later. Can product/obs/finance confirm:
- what's feasible in the next 2–3 weeks for a CSV export?
- effort to add a per-route dashboard widget (filterable by customer, model, time window)?
- any billing attribution constraints we should flag to customer?

Thanks — I can sync them to a short demo once we have a proposal.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Route-level insights / attribution request from Acme AI

Thanks Sean — good summary. A few quick clarifying Qs before we scope: 
1) When they say "route" do they mean HTTP path only, or do they include query/metadata that changes model selection? (If it's just the path we can probably map to an existing request tag.)
2) Do they need historical retroactive attribution for past months (billing reconciliation) or only forward-looking exports?

On feasibility:
- CSV export of aggregated per-route daily tokens & cost: medium effort. We can produce a csv from existing aggregation tables if we have stable route tags attached to telemetry. ETA: prototype CSV endpoint in ~2 weeks if obs can confirm tag availability.
- Interactive dashboard: depends on whether we can reuse the existing per-customer pane and add route as a dimension. If yes, ETA 4–6 weeks for an MVP (filtering + timeseries).

I'll open a Jira to track (OBS-428) and tag obs/infra. Marissa — can you validate whether route tags exist consistently in the logs and whether KV cache/batching complicates attribution? Karthik — any concerns on invoice/retroactive attributions?

-Laura

Quick readout from the observability side: 
- Route tagging: we have 3 ways requests are labeled today: endpoint path, user-supplied route tag (opt-in header), and internal router label (added by api-gateway). In practice the gateway label is present for ~92% of traffic. That should be sufficient for an initial CSV so long as the customer uses standard paths.
- Attribution edge cases: batching and shared cached prefixes mean a little of the token accounting could be amortized across requests — we can still report "attributed tokens" (what we charge to a route) but need to call out the caveat in docs.
- Dashboard approach: propose adding a "Route Insights" card to the per-customer dashboard that shows: top 10 routes by cost, time series tokens & cost, p50/p95 latency. I attached a quick mockup (route-dashboard-mockup-v1.png).

To move fast:
1) We can deliver a CSV export endpoint that runs as an on-demand job against daily aggregates (prototype in ~2 weeks).
2) CSV will include: date, route_label, model_variant, tokens, cost_usd, p50_ms, p95_ms, request_count.
3) MVP dashboard (filterable by date + route) target 4 weeks if we reuse existing UI components.

I'll link OBS-428 with some notes and drop a PR for the CSV schema. If product wants this prioritized higher, we should move to a canary/expedite lane.

— Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Route-level insights / attribution request from Acme AI

Couple notes from finance/billing: 
- For invoicing we need a stable identifier that we can tie to ledger entries. If route_label may change (customer-side renames), we need a canonical route_id in telemetry (immutable) or a mapping table.
- Retroactive attribution: expensive. We can try to re-run aggregation jobs for a reconciliation quarter but it will be manual and billable effort. We should clarify whether Acme expects retroactive corrections.
- Pricing implication: if customers want per-route unit pricing, that will require recording which route initiated model selection at the time of each token generation — which is feasible but will increase storage/ingest cost.

I recommend we offer: (A) forward-looking CSV export + dashboard; (B) optional one-time retroactive reconciliation as a paid service. Sean — can you confirm whether Acme expects past-month adjustments? Also cc procurement if we move toward a paid reconciliation.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Finance, Redwood Inference
